 What Airbnb Holders Got Right
 October 28, 2026 SI Simply Wall St Reviewed by Bailey Pemberton If Airbnb was on your watchlist instead of in your portfolio, the recent move may feel expensive in hindsight. For Airbnb shareholders, the return over the past year was 31.9%, including dividends. That result invites a tougher question. Back on 27 October 2025, what could have helped you spot the potential in a travel app that was trying to become a broader lifestyle and services platform, and how confident could you reasonably be in that business shift?
 The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.
 Airbnb has already moved. See which of 29 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.
 Advertisement The Two Stories Airbnb Investors Had In Front Of Them
 The shares cost US$129 at the start of the period, which meant any view on Airbnb needed a clear story about where the business could sensibly head next.
 The bullish narrative put fair value at US$164, 27% above the start price. It relied on revenue growing 12.0% a year and profit margins reaching 25.0% within a three-year window, supported by international expansion, long-term rentals and heavy use of AI across the platform.
 The bearish view set fair value at US$96, 26% below the start price. That story focused on tightening regulations, especially in Europe, pressure on host economics, and the risk that vacation rentals in North America and Western Europe were already close to saturation.
 NasdaqGS:ABNB 1-Year Stock Price Chart What The Evidence Around Airbnb Actually Tested
 Airbnb’s push to become a broader services platform showed up in the period through hotel offerings, Reserve Now, Pay Later and a ramped up AI lab, all of which leaned toward the bullish story of a richer, higher margin ecosystem. Rising regulatory pressure, including Chicago’s lawsuit and tighter city rules, pushed back toward the cautious case. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.
 The lesson is simple. When a platform promises a new profit engine, you can test it later by checking segment disclosures, product launches and whether reported margins actually move toward the original target.
 What Airbnb's Current Price Already Bakes In
 Airbnb now trades at US$169, after a 31.9% gain over the past year. This Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level, which signals that its author sees today’s quote as already reflecting a confident set of business expectations.
 The pitch is that an AI native rebuild, hotels and services together keep bookings and profitability resilient even if new travel agents or rules bite. A buyer at today’s price is effectively assuming those AI driven efficiencies and new categories offset regulatory and intermediary risks. How does that stack up against the source Narrative’s concerns about future margin pressure?
 "While Airbnb is rebuilding its platform to be AI native with faster feature releases and lower customer support cost per booking, a portion of these efficiency gains may need to be reinvested into pricing, safety, and service to defend against AI driven travel agents and other intermediaries. This could cap future net margin expansion." Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the lower figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there 
 Another Way Travelers Prepay
 Airbnb shows what happens when guests pay upfront for future stays. Another travel intermediary leans heavily on the same idea.
 Instead of rooms listed by individual hosts, it routes bookings to traditional hotels and other providers. Customers still hand over cash long before trips actually happen.
 During that gap, the operator holds large balances that resemble spare liquidity. In reality, they are obligations waiting for check in dates.
 If you are weighing Airbnb’s platform risk, it helps to see how this other travel middleman handles its own float when seasons turn.
 It is written up in full, assumptions and all. → Explore the Narrative that puts this company 115% above its price
